items.title: A Rainy Saturday
items.text: Last Saturday it rained all day, so my brother Minho and I could not go to the park. At first we were bored. Then our mother brought out a box of old photos from the closet. We sat on the floor and looked at pictures of our grandparents when they were young. In one photo, our grandfather was holding a huge fish and smiling proudly. Minho laughed and said it looked bigger than a small dog. By evening, we had made a little album of our favorite pictures. It turned out to be a very nice day, even without the park.

qs.q: What is the passage mainly about?
o: Two boys learned how to catch a fish from their mother.
Two boys found a fun indoor activity on a rainy day.
A family trip to the park was canceled by a storm.
A mother cleaned the closet and threw away old photos.
qs.why: 비 오는 날 집에서 사진을 보며 즐겁게 보낸 이야기예요.

qs.q: Where did the boys look at the old photos?
o: On the floor
In the park
In the closet
At school
qs.why: “We sat on the floor and looked at pictures.”

qs.q: In the passage, the word “huge” is closest in meaning to
o: very fresh
very cheap
very quiet
very big
qs.why: 물고기가 작은 개보다 크다고 했으니 huge는 ‘아주 큰’이에요.

qs.q: How did the writer feel at the end of the day?
o: Sad that the album was not finished
Angry that the park trip was canceled
Glad that the day turned out well
Worried that the photos were so old
qs.why: 마지막 문장에서 비 오는 날이 매우 좋은 하루가 되었다고 했어요.

items.title: The Recycling Club
items.text: Our school started a recycling club in March. Every Wednesday, about twenty students meet after lunch and check the bins near the cafeteria. They take out bottles and cans that were thrown into the wrong bin. The club leader, Ms. Han, says the problem is not that students are lazy. Many of them simply do not know which items can be recycled. So the club made colorful signs with pictures and put them above every bin. Since then, the number of mistakes has dropped by almost half. Next month, the club plans to visit a recycling center to see what happens to the plastic.

qs.q: Why did the club make the colorful signs?
o: Students wanted to decorate the cafeteria walls.
Students did not know what goes into each bin.
Ms. Han wanted to teach art to the new members.
The school had too few bins for all the students.
qs.why: 클럽장은 학생들이 재활용 방법을 몰라서 실수한다고 설명했어요. 그래서 그림 표지판을 만들었어요.

qs.q: When does the club meet?
o: On Wednesdays after lunch
On Fridays after school
Every morning before class
On Wednesdays before lunch
qs.why: “Every Wednesday ... meet after lunch”

qs.q: What can we infer about the signs?
o: They were too difficult for students to understand.
They made the cafeteria much louder than before.
They were removed after the club visited the center.
They helped students use the bins more correctly.
qs.why: 실수가 거의 절반으로 줄었다는 내용에서 표지판이 효과가 있었음을 알 수 있어요.

qs.q: Which is NOT true according to the passage?
o: The club leader is named Ms. Han.
About twenty students join the meetings.
The club has already visited a recycling center.
The club began at the start of spring.
qs.why: 재활용 센터 방문은 다음 달 계획이에요. (March는 봄의 시작)

items.title: Why Teenagers Need Sleep
items.text: Many teenagers stay up late to study, play games, or chat with friends. However, doctors say that people between thirteen and eighteen need about nine hours of sleep each night. During sleep, the brain stores what we learned during the day. When teenagers sleep too little, they find it harder to pay attention in class, and they may also feel angry more easily. One simple tip is to turn off screens an hour before bed. Reading a book or listening to quiet music can help the body relax. Good sleep is not a waste of time. It is part of staying healthy and doing well at school.

qs.q: What is the best title for the passage?
o: Games Are Bad for the Brain
Sleep Is Important for Teenagers
How to Study Until Midnight
Why Doctors Read Books at Night
qs.why: 십 대에게 잠이 왜 필요한지와 방법을 설명하는 글이에요.

qs.q: According to the passage, what happens when teenagers sleep too little?
o: They may find it hard to pay attention.
They usually grow taller very quickly.
They remember everything better than before.
They stop wanting to talk with their friends.
qs.why: “they find it harder to pay attention in class”

qs.q: Why does the writer mention reading a book?
o: To say that books are better than school
To explain why the brain stores memories
To warn readers about reading too much
To suggest a way to relax at night
qs.why: 책 읽기는 자기 전에 몸을 쉬게 하는 방법으로 소개됐어요.

qs.q: In the passage, “However” introduces
o: a result of the idea before it
an example of the idea before it
a contrast with the idea before it
a time order of the ideas before it
qs.why: 앞에서는 늦게까지 깨어 있는 모습, 뒤에서는 의사들의 반대 의견이라 대조예요.

items.title: Busy as a Bee
items.text: A honeybee looks small, but it works very hard. A worker bee visits hundreds of flowers in one trip to collect sweet liquid called nectar. It carries the nectar back to the hive in a special stomach. There, other bees turn it into honey. To make just one spoonful of honey, twelve bees must work their whole lives. Bees also help plants. When they move from flower to flower, they carry a yellow powder called pollen, and this helps the plants make seeds and fruit. Without bees, we would have fewer apples, almonds, and many other foods on our tables.

qs.q: What is the main idea of the passage?
o: Honey is the most delicious food in the world.
Bees work hard and are useful to people and plants.
Flowers grow only in places where bees live.
Bees are dangerous and should stay away from homes.
qs.why: 꿀벌의 부지런함과 식물·사람에게 주는 도움이 중심 내용이에요.

qs.q: What do other bees do in the hive?
o: They change nectar into honey.
They carry pollen to the flowers.
They look for new places to live.
They count the visitors to each flower.
qs.why: “There, other bees turn it into honey.”

qs.q: In the passage, “this” in “this helps the plants” refers to
o: making one spoonful of honey
visiting hundreds of flowers on one trip
turning nectar into honey in the hive
carrying pollen from flower to flower
qs.why: 앞 문장의 pollen을 옮기는 일을 가리켜요.

qs.q: What can we infer from the last sentence?
o: People should stop eating fruit and nuts.
Bees only visit apple and almond trees.
Many foods depend on the work of bees.
Honey is more useful than every other food.
qs.why: 벌이 없으면 사과, 아몬드 등이 줄어든다는 말에서 많은 음식이 벌에 달려 있음을 알 수 있어요.

items.title: Early at the Bakery
items.text: Mr. Park wakes up at three o'clock every morning, long before the sun rises. He walks to his small bakery and turns on the ovens. First he mixes the dough for bread, and then he shapes it into loaves and rolls. By five thirty, the smell of fresh bread fills the street. Many neighbors stop by on their way to work to buy something warm to eat. Although the job is tiring, Mr. Park says he loves it. He enjoys seeing people smile when they take their first bite. On Sundays, he gives away the bread that is left to families who need it.

qs.q: What does Mr. Park do right after he arrives at the bakery?
o: He mixes dough for the neighbors.
He turns on the ovens.
He gives bread to people in need.
He opens the doors for customers.
qs.why: “walks to his small bakery and turns on the ovens”

qs.q: What is the passage mainly about?
o: A baker's early work and why he likes it
A neighborhood that has too many busy bakeries
The best way to cook fresh bread at home
A man who is tired of getting up so early
qs.why: 제빵사의 이른 아침 일과와 일을 좋아하는 이유가 중심이에요.

qs.q: Why does the writer say “Although the job is tiring”?
o: To explain why Mr. Park will close the shop
To prove that bread is hard to make
To tell readers not to buy bread early
To show that Mr. Park still likes his work
qs.why: Although 뒤에 힘들어도 좋아한다는 대조가 이어져요.

qs.q: What does Mr. Park do on Sundays?
o: He sells bread at a lower price.
He teaches neighbors to bake rolls.
He gives leftover bread to families.
He stays at home and sleeps late.
qs.why: “On Sundays, he gives away the bread that is left.”

items.title: Sharing Bikes in the City
items.text: In our city, there is a new bike-sharing program. People can borrow a bike from one station and return it to any other station. All they need is a phone and a small payment, which is less than the price of a bus ticket. The program began last spring with fifty stations, and now there are almost two hundred. City officials say that the bikes help reduce traffic and air pollution. Some people, however, are worried. They say that many riders do not wear helmets and that the bikes are often left on the sidewalk. The city has promised to build more bike lanes and to teach riders the rules.

qs.q: How can people borrow a bike?
o: With a bus ticket from the station
With a phone and a small payment
With a helmet from a city officer
With a letter from their school
qs.why: “All they need is a phone and a small payment.”

qs.q: What is the writer's main purpose?
o: To explain a new program and its problems
To ask readers to buy a bicycle this coming spring
To prove that city bus tickets cost far too much
To show how to repair a broken bike at home
qs.why: 자전거 공유 제도와 그에 대한 우려를 함께 소개하는 글이에요.

qs.q: According to the passage, what is one problem?
o: The stations are far from every bus stop.
Riders must pay before each short trip.
There are only fifty bikes in the city.
Bikes are often left on the sidewalk.
qs.why: “the bikes are often left on the sidewalk”

qs.q: What can we infer about the program?
o: It will end before next spring.
It is used only by city officials.
It has grown quickly since it started.
It has no support from the city.
qs.why: 50개 정류장에서 약 200개로 늘었다는 것에서 빠르게 커졌음을 알 수 있어요.

items.title: A Notice About the Field Trip
items.text: Dear parents, our school trip to the Science Museum will be on Friday, May 16. Students should arrive at school by 8:30 a.m. because the bus will leave at 9:00. Please make sure your child brings a lunch box, a water bottle, and a notebook. Snacks are welcome, but candy and soda are not allowed on the bus. The museum has a special show about space, which will begin at 1:00 p.m. We expect to return to school at about 4:00 p.m. If your child has any health problems, please write to the homeroom teacher by next Monday. Thank you for your help.

qs.q: Why was this notice written?
o: To ask parents to buy tickets for a space show
To give parents information about a school trip
To announce that the museum will close early
To tell students about a change in the bus route
qs.why: 현장학습 준비 사항과 일정을 알리는 안내문이에요.

qs.q: What time will the bus leave?
qs.why: “the bus will leave at 9:00”

qs.q: Which item is NOT allowed on the bus?
o: A notebook
A lunch box
A water bottle
Soda
qs.why: 사탕과 탄산음료는 버스에서 안 된다고 했어요.

qs.q: What should parents do if their child has a health problem?
o: Call the museum on the day of the trip
Bring the child to school before 8:30
Write to the homeroom teacher by Monday
Send a doctor's letter to the bus driver
qs.why: “write to the homeroom teacher by next Monday”

items.title: Letter from a Pen Pal
items.text: Dear Sora, thank you for your last letter. I was happy to hear that you joined the school band. Here in Canada, winter has just started, and everything is white with snow. On weekends, my friends and I go to a frozen lake near my house. We skate for hours and drink hot chocolate afterward. I am not very good at skating yet, so I fall down a lot, but it is still fun. Do you have snow in Korea in December? Please tell me about your favorite winter activity. I have also sent a small package with some maple candy. I hope you like it. Your friend, Emma

o: To invite Sora to join her school band

To complain that the winter was too cold

qs.q: What does Emma do on weekends in winter?

qs.q: What did Emma send to Sora?

A pair of warm skates
A package with candy
A book about Canada
qs.why: “I have also sent a small package with some maple candy.”

items.title: A Day at the Art Museum
items.text: Last weekend, our class visited the city art museum. The guide first showed us a painting of a quiet village by the sea. She explained that the artist used soft blue and gray colors to make the picture feel calm. In the next room, there were large statues made of metal. Some of us touched them by mistake, and the guide told us gently to keep our hands to ourselves. My favorite part was the children's room, where we could draw our own pictures and hang them on the wall. I was surprised to learn that many famous artists began drawing when they were very young. I want to visit again soon.

qs.q: Why did the artist use soft blue and gray colors?
o: To show a storm over the village
To make the picture feel calm
To save money on expensive paint
To match the color of the statues
qs.why: “used soft blue and gray colors to make the picture feel calm”

o: Some students touched them, and the guide spoke kindly.
The guide asked every student to draw the statues.

Looking at the painting by the sea
Buying a gift in the museum shop
Drawing pictures in the children's room

Interested and eager to go again
Angry about the guide's advice

items.title: Should Phones Be Allowed in Class?
items.text: Some schools let students use phones in class, and others do not. People who support phones say that students can look up words quickly and take photos of the board. Phones can also be useful in emergencies. On the other hand, many teachers worry that phones take attention away from learning. A student may check messages or play a game instead of listening. In one school, students keep their phones in a box at the front of the room and take them back when the lesson ends. Teachers there say the students talk to each other more. I think a middle way is best: phones can be used only when the teacher asks.

qs.q: What does the writer think?
o: Phones should be banned in every school.
Phones should be used only when asked.
Students should always keep phones on the desk.
Teachers should use games in every single lesson.
qs.why: 마지막 문장에 글쓴이의 의견이 나와요.

qs.q: What is one reason given for allowing phones?

Students can play games after class.

o: Students lose their phones every day.

Students use phones in every lesson.
Students talk to each other more.
qs.why: “Teachers there say the students talk to each other more.”

o: a reason for the first idea
the end of the story
a different point of view
a time before the first idea
qs.why: 반대 입장을 소개하는 연결어예요.

items.title: Life in the Cold
items.text: Emperor penguins live in Antarctica, one of the coldest places on Earth. In winter, the temperature can fall below minus forty degrees. To stay warm, the penguins stand very close together in a large group. They take turns standing at the outside of the group, where it is coldest, and then move slowly to the warm middle. In this way, no penguin has to stay in the cold for too long. The fathers also keep an egg on their feet under a warm fold of skin for about two months while the mothers are away looking for food. This teamwork helps the baby penguins to be born safely.

qs.q: What is the passage mainly about?
o: Why Antarctica is the coldest place on Earth
How penguins work together to survive the cold
How fathers and mothers choose their names
Where penguins find food in the summer

o: On their feet
Under the snow
In the warm middle
Inside a nest of stones
qs.why: “keep an egg on their feet under a warm fold of skin”

o: So that they can watch for hungry animals
So that the babies can learn to swim
So that the middle penguins can sleep
So that no one stays in the cold for too long
qs.why: “no penguin has to stay in the cold for too long”

qs.q: What are the mothers doing while the fathers keep the eggs?
o: Standing in the warm middle
Playing with the baby penguins
Looking for food
Building a place to sleep
qs.why: “while the mothers are away looking for food”

items.title: My First Week at a New School
items.text: I started at a new school on Monday. On the first day, I was so nervous that I could hardly eat breakfast. I did not know anyone, and the hallways looked like a maze. In my first class, the teacher asked me to introduce myself. My voice shook, but when I said that I liked playing the drums, a boy named Jihun smiled at me. At lunch, he invited me to sit with his friends. By Friday, I knew where every classroom was. Now I feel much more comfortable. I learned that a new place becomes easier when someone is kind to you.

qs.q: How did the writer feel on the first day?
o: Proud and full of energy
Nervous and a little lost
Bored and tired of school
Angry at the new teacher
qs.why: 아침을 거의 못 먹을 만큼 긴장했고 복도도 미로 같다고 했어요.

qs.q: Why did Jihun smile at the writer?
o: The writer said he liked playing the drums.
The writer told a funny story to the class.
The writer knew all the answers in class.
The writer gave him a gift at lunch.
qs.why: 드럼을 좋아한다고 말하자 지훈이 미소 지었어요.

qs.q: In the passage, “maze” suggests that the hallways were
o: clean and bright
empty and quiet
wide and noisy
hard to find one's way

Kindness from others makes a new place easier.
A good breakfast is the key to a good day.

items.title: Monsoon Season
items.text: In many parts of Asia, summer brings the monsoon, a season of heavy rain. The word comes from an Arabic word that means “season.” Warm, wet winds blow from the ocean toward the land, and the sky stays gray for weeks. For farmers, the rain is a gift because rice needs a lot of water to grow. However, too much rain can cause floods that damage houses and roads. People prepare by cleaning drains, keeping an umbrella ready, and checking weather reports every day. Children often enjoy the season too. They jump in puddles and listen to the sound of rain on the roof.

qs.q: Why is the monsoon rain a gift for farmers?
o: Floods make the roads easier to use.
Rice needs a lot of water to grow.
The gray sky keeps the fields warm.
Farmers can rest while it rains.
qs.why: “rice needs a lot of water to grow”

qs.q: What can too much rain cause?
o: Floods that damage houses and roads
Strong winds that blow the roofs off
Shorter summers all across Asia
Drains that slowly start to grow rice
qs.why: “too much rain can cause floods that damage houses and roads”

qs.q: Which sentence best summarizes the passage?

Children are afraid of the rainy season.
Weather reports are always wrong in summer.
The monsoon brings both benefits and problems.
qs.why: 장마의 장점과 문제점을 함께 다뤄요.

qs.q: What does the word “monsoon” originally mean?
o: Heavy rain
Warm wind
Season
Puddle
qs.why: “an Arabic word that means ‘season’”

items.title: A Robot Vacuum Review
items.text: I bought this robot vacuum two months ago, and I am mostly happy with it. It moves around the living room by itself and picks up dust and pet hair. My dog's hair used to cover the floor, but now it is clean every evening. The battery lasts about ninety minutes, which is enough for our small apartment. However, the vacuum sometimes gets stuck under the sofa and makes a loud beeping sound. It also cannot climb the small step at the kitchen door. For a family with a busy schedule, it saves time. I would give it four stars out of five and recommend it to people who live in small homes.

qs.q: Why does the writer give four stars instead of five?
o: The vacuum cost too much money.
The vacuum has a few small problems.
The battery lasts only ten minutes.
The vacuum does not pick up dust.
qs.why: 소파 밑에 끼고 문턱을 못 넘는 등 작은 문제가 있어요.

qs.q: According to the review, what is one good point?

qs.why: 리뷰에서 로봇청소기가 스스로 먼지와 털을 치워 매일 저녁 바닥이 깨끗하다는 장점을 말했어요.

qs.q: Who would the writer recommend this vacuum to?
o: People who have no pets
People with many stairs
People who dislike beeping
People living in small homes
qs.why: “recommend it to people who live in small homes”

qs.q: What is the purpose of this text?
o: To explain how robots are made
To advertise a new pet shop
To give an opinion about a product
To tell a story about a dog

items.title: Sports Day
items.text: Every October, our school holds Sports Day. The students are divided into a blue team and a white team. In the morning, we run races and play tug-of-war. After lunch, there is a big relay race, which is the most exciting event. This year, I was the last runner for the blue team. When I took the stick, we were behind by about ten meters. My heart beat fast, and my legs felt heavy, but I kept running. Near the end, I passed the white runner and crossed the line first. My teammates jumped up and shouted. Even though the white team won the tug-of-war, the relay was the moment I will remember.

qs.q: Which event does the writer think is the most exciting?
o: The tug-of-war
The relay race
The morning races
The lunch break
qs.why: “a big relay race, which is the most exciting event”

qs.q: How did the writer feel when taking the stick?

Calm because the team was ahead
Tired because the race was long
Surprised because the stick was lost
qs.why: 약 10미터 뒤처져 있어서 심장이 빨리 뛰고 다리가 무거웠다고 했으니 긴장한 거예요.

The writer passed the white runner.

qs.q: What does “Even though” show in the last sentence?
o: A reason for the white team's win

A contrast between two results
An example of a team game

items.title: Volunteers at the Animal Shelter
items.text: Every second Saturday, a group of high school and middle school students helps at the Happy Paws animal shelter. Some of them walk the dogs in the yard, while others clean the cages and fill the water bowls. A volunteer named Yuna says the most important job is playing with the cats. Many of the cats were once lost or hurt, so they are shy at first. When people speak softly and sit quietly, the cats slowly come closer. The shelter does not have enough money to hire many workers, so the volunteers are a big help. In the last year, more than eighty animals found new homes.

o: The animals need to learn to walk alone.
The shelter cannot pay for many workers.
The cats do not like the shelter staff.
The students want to become doctors.
qs.why: “does not have enough money to hire many workers”

qs.q: What does Yuna say is the most important job?
o: Playing with the cats
Walking the dogs
Cleaning the cages
Filling the water bowls
qs.why: “the most important job is playing with the cats”

qs.q: Why are many of the cats shy?
o: They are afraid of dogs in the yard.
They have never seen a person.
They do not like quiet voices.
They were once lost or hurt.
qs.why: “Many of the cats were once lost or hurt, so they are shy”

qs.q: What is the passage mainly about?
o: A shelter that sells cats and dogs
A teacher who loves cleaning cages
Students who help animals at a shelter
A town where nobody keeps pets

items.title: Water, the Best Drink
items.text: Our bodies are about sixty percent water, so we need to drink enough every day. Water helps carry food energy around the body, keeps the skin healthy, and controls body temperature. Doctors usually advise teenagers to drink six to eight glasses a day, and more on hot days or after sports. Some people choose juice or soda instead, but these drinks often contain a lot of sugar. One easy habit is to carry a water bottle and take a few sips every hour. If your urine is a pale yellow color, you are probably drinking enough. If it is dark, you should drink more.

To explain why skin gets dry on hot days
To list the drinks that doctors sell here

Choosing juice after every game
Counting glasses in the school cafeteria

Sports for Hot Summer Days
Drink Enough Water Every Day
How Doctors Test the Body

items.title: Night Market Adventure
items.text: On our trip to Taiwan, my family visited a night market near our hotel. The street was crowded with people, and the air was full of the smell of fried chicken, sweet tea, and grilled corn. My little sister wanted to try everything, but my father said we should share, so we could taste more kinds of food. I tried stinky tofu for the first time. The smell was strong, but the taste was surprisingly good. We also played a game where you throw rings onto bottles, and my mother won a small toy panda. We stayed until almost eleven o'clock. It was tiring but unforgettable, and I hope to go back one day.

qs.q: Why did the writer's father say they should share food?
o: To spend less time at the market
To taste more kinds of food
To avoid the smell of tofu
To keep the little sister quiet

The writer's sister
The writer
The writer's mother

The family was sorry about the trip.

The food was not worth the money.

items.title: Chuseok Traditions
items.text: Chuseok is one of the biggest holidays in Korea. Families travel to their hometowns to see their relatives, and the roads are often full of cars. On the morning of Chuseok, people prepare a table of food to thank their ancestors for the harvest. Afterwards, the whole family eats together. A special food is songpyeon, a half-moon rice cake filled with sesame or sweet beans. Children often help to shape the cakes by hand. In the evening, people look at the full moon and make wishes. For many Koreans, the holiday is a time to be thankful and to feel close to family.

qs.q: What is Chuseok mainly a time for?
o: Learning new things at school
Giving thanks and being with family
Racing cars on the roads
Selling rice cakes in markets

qs.q: What is songpyeon?
o: A rice cake with sesame or beans inside
A special table set for the ancestors
A game that people play under the moon
A dish that is made of fried fish

To celebrate the full moon alone

To thank their ancestors for the harvest

Many people travel at the same time.

items.title: The Lost Wallet
items.text: On the way home from school, Hajun saw a brown wallet on the sidewalk. He picked it up and looked inside. There was some money and a card with the name of a man and a phone number. Hajun thought about keeping the money for a new pair of sneakers, but he felt uneasy. He remembered how worried he was when he lost his own bag last year. So he called the number from his phone. The man answered happily and came to meet him in ten minutes. He tried to give Hajun some money as thanks, but Hajun smiled and said no. That night, he slept very well.

Doing the right thing can make us feel good.
New sneakers are worth any price.

items.title: Coral Reefs
items.text: Coral reefs cover less than one percent of the ocean floor, but about a quarter of all sea animals live in or near them. A reef is built by tiny animals called corals. They grow slowly, and some reefs are thousands of years old. Many fish find food and shelter among the corals. However, reefs are in danger. When the sea gets too warm, the corals turn white and may die. Pollution and careless fishing also harm them. Scientists are now growing young corals in tanks and placing them back in the sea. People can help, too, by using less plastic and by never touching the reef when they swim.

The corals grow much faster.
The fish move into the tanks.

Catching the fish that harm the reef
Moving old reefs onto the sandy beach
Growing young corals and returning them

They are made by large fish.

qs.why: 바다 동물의 4분의 1이 산호초 근처에 살지만 바닥의 1퍼센트 미만이에요.

items.title: Staying Safe Online
items.text: The internet is a great place to learn and talk to friends, but it also has risks. First, never share your password with anyone except your parents. A strong password is long and uses letters, numbers, and signs. Second, be careful about what you post. Photos of your school or your home address can tell strangers where to find you. Third, if someone you do not know sends you a message, do not answer it. Tell an adult you trust instead. Finally, remember that people online may not be who they say they are. If something feels strange, you can always stop and ask for help.

qs.q: Why should students avoid posting their home address?
o: Friends might forget where they live.
Strangers could learn where to find them.

qs.why: 주소나 학교 사진이 낯선 사람에게 위치를 알려 줄 수 있어요.

o: Your parents
Your classmates

Your teachers
qs.why: “except your parents”

qs.q: What is the writer's purpose?

To explain how strong passwords are made
To sell a safety program for parents
To give advice on safe internet use
qs.why: 인터넷을 안전하게 쓰는 방법을 조언해요.

items.title: School Festival Schedule
items.text: The school festival will be held on October 24. The opening ceremony begins at 9:30 in the main hall. items.title: The Chef Who Hated Cooking
items.text: When Minseo was young, she hated cooking. Her grandmother ran a small restaurant, and Minseo thought the kitchen was hot, noisy, and boring. One summer, her grandmother had a hurt arm and asked Minseo for help. At first, Minseo only washed vegetables. Little by little, she began to notice how a simple pinch of salt could change a soup. She asked questions, tasted dishes, and tried small experiments. When her grandmother's arm healed, Minseo did not want to leave the kitchen. Today she is a chef in a busy city restaurant. She often says that her first teacher was a woman who needed an extra pair of hands.

o: She felt it was a calm place to rest.
She thought it was hot and boring.
She found it quiet and cool, like a library.

Watching cooking shows at home every night
Winning a cooking prize at school
Seeing how a little salt changed a soup

items.title: How a Rainbow Forms
items.text: A rainbow appears when sunlight passes through tiny drops of water in the air. The light slows down as it enters each drop and bends. Inside the drop, it bounces off the back and comes out again, bending a second time. Because each color bends by a slightly different amount, the white sunlight splits into red, orange, yellow, green, blue, and purple. To see a rainbow, you must stand with the sun behind you and the rain in front of you. That is why rainbows often appear in the afternoon or early morning, when the sun is low in the sky.

qs.q: What is needed to make a rainbow?
o: Strong wind and dark storm clouds
Sunlight and drops of water in the air

The back of the drop is dark.

With the sun behind you

items.title: Bus Route Changes
items.text: Starting Monday, March 3, Bus 17 will use a new route. Instead of going along River Road, the bus will turn left at the post office and stop at Central Park. Passengers who need these stops can take Bus 22 or walk for about five minutes. The city office says that the change was made because the old road is going to be repaired. items.title: Learning the Guitar
items.text: Last year, I got a guitar for my birthday. I was very excited, but my fingers hurt after only ten minutes of practice. I wanted to quit. My older cousin told me that every player begins with sore fingers. He showed me three easy chords and said, “Play them for five minutes a day, but do it every day.” I followed his advice. After a month, my fingers became harder, and I could play a simple song. Now I practice for half an hour after dinner. I have learned that small steps are better than one huge effort. Next week I will play for my family at my grandmother's birthday party.

items.title: Climbing Mount Halla
items.text: Mount Halla is the highest mountain in South Korea. It stands on Jeju Island and is about 1,950 meters tall. There are several trails to the top. The Seongpanak trail is the longest, but it is also the easiest, with a gentle slope. Hikers need about four hours to climb up and another three to come down. Because the weather can change quickly, visitors are advised to bring warm clothes, even in summer. At the top, there is a small crater lake. On a clear day, the view across the island and the sea is wonderful. Many people say the hard climb is worth it when they reach the top.

items.title: The Plastic Bag Problem
items.text: Every minute, about a million plastic bags are used around the world. Most are used for only a few minutes, but they can stay in nature for hundreds of years. Animals sometimes eat the bags by mistake, and this can make them sick. To solve the problem, some countries now ask shoppers to pay a small fee for each bag. items.title: Grandmother's Garden
items.text: My grandmother has a small garden behind her house. Every spring, she plants tomatoes, lettuce, and peppers. She wakes up early to water them before the sun gets too hot. I think her garden is more than a place for plants. It is a place where people become friends.

items.title: Before the Talent Show

items.title: The Time Capsule
items.text: Last June, our class made a time capsule. We put a letter to ourselves, a photo of the class, and a list of our favorite songs in a metal box. items.title: A Quiet Neighbor
items.text: When we first moved to our building, we thought the old man in the next apartment was unfriendly. He never said hello in the elevator, and his door was always shut. One day, my mother baked a cake and knocked on his door. He opened it slowly, looked surprised, and then smiled. He told us that his hearing is poor and that he is shy about speaking because people often have to repeat themselves. Since then, we leave notes on his door, and he answers with small drawings. Last week, he gave us a tiny plant in a cup. It is on our window, and we call it our friendship plant.

He had just moved into the building.
qs.why: 청력이 나쁘고 말하기를 부끄러워했어요.

qs.q: What did the writer's mother do?
o: She brought him a cake.
She wrote him a long letter.
She asked him to move away.
She gave him a plant.
qs.why: 케이크를 구워 문을 두드렸어요.

qs.q: How do the neighbors talk now?
o: By calling on the phone
By meeting in the elevator
By shouting through the wall
By leaving notes and drawings
qs.why: 쪽지와 그림으로 소통해요.

qs.q: What is the main point?
o: Old people always prefer to live in silence.
Cakes can solve every problem between neighbors.
First impressions can change as we understand people.
Plants grow well in small apartments with windows.
qs.why: 처음 인상이 이해로 바뀐 이야기예요.

items.title: Why Cats Purr
items.text: Most people think that cats purr only when they are happy. In fact, cats purr for several reasons. A kitten purrs to tell its mother that it is safe and warm while it drinks milk. An adult cat may purr when it is relaxed on a sofa. Surprisingly, some cats also purr when they are hurt, scared, or at the animal doctor. Scientists believe that the soft vibration may help calm the cat and even help its bones heal. So when you hear a purr, look at the cat's body as well. A cat with a stiff tail and wide eyes may need comfort rather than play.

qs.q: What is the main idea of the passage?
o: Kittens purr louder than adult cats.
Purring has more than one meaning for cats.
Cats purr only when they are hungry.
Animal doctors teach cats to purr.
qs.why: 고양이가 가르랑거리는 이유가 여러 가지임을 설명해요.

qs.q: Why does a kitten purr while it drinks milk?
o: To tell its mother it is safe and warm
To ask its mother for more food right away
To call the other kittens to the milk
To keep its own little bones warm
qs.why: “to tell its mother that it is safe and warm”

qs.q: What do scientists believe about the vibration?
o: It may keep other cats far away.
It may make the cat feel sleepy at night.
It may hide how scared the cat feels.
It may calm the cat and help its bones.
qs.why: “help calm the cat and even help its bones heal”

qs.q: Why does the writer say to look at the cat's body?
o: A cat's body shows how heavy it is.
Cats cannot purr without moving their tails.
A purr alone does not always show happiness.
The tail tells how old the cat is.
qs.why: 가르랑거림만으로는 기분을 알 수 없다는 뜻이에요.

items.title: The Library Card Advertisement
items.text: Do you love stories, music, or games? Then get a free library card today! With your card, you can borrow up to ten books for three weeks. You can also borrow movies and music CDs, and use the computers in our new study room. Every Saturday at 11:00, there is a story hour for children, and on the first Friday of each month, we hold a book club for teenagers. To get a card, just bring an ID with your name and address to the front desk. Parents must sign for children under fourteen. Come and discover how many adventures are waiting for you on our shelves!

qs.q: What is the purpose of this text?
o: To ask readers to donate their old books
To encourage people to get a library card
To announce that the library will close soon
To explain how to repair a library computer
qs.why: 도서관 카드 발급을 홍보하는 글이에요.

qs.q: How many books can a card holder borrow?
o: Up to ten
Up to three
Up to fourteen
As many as they like
qs.why: “borrow up to ten books for three weeks”

qs.q: When is the book club for teenagers?
o: Every Saturday at 11:00
On the last day of each month
Every Friday after school
On the first Friday of each month
qs.why: 매달 첫째 금요일이에요.

qs.q: Who must sign for a library card?
o: Teachers of every child
All teenagers in the book club
Parents of children under fourteen
Adults who borrow movies
qs.why: “Parents must sign for children under fourteen.”

items.title: Ordering Lunch
items.text:
Waiter: Good afternoon. Are you ready to order?
Jina: Yes. I would like the chicken salad, please.
Waiter: Certainly. Would you like soup or a drink with that?
Jina: Is the soup made with milk? I am allergic to dairy.
Waiter: The tomato soup is dairy free, but the mushroom soup has cream.
Jina: Then I will have the tomato soup, please.
Waiter: Great. Anything to drink?
Jina: Just water, thank you.
Waiter: Your food will be ready in about ten minutes.

qs.q: Why does Jina ask about the soup?
o: She dislikes tomatoes.
She cannot have dairy foods.
She wants a cheaper meal.
She is in a hurry.
qs.why: 우유 알레르기가 있다고 했어요.

qs.q: Which soup does Jina choose?
o: The tomato soup
The mushroom soup
The chicken soup
No soup
qs.why: 토마토 수프가 유제품이 없어서 골랐어요.

qs.q: What does Jina drink?
o: Milk
Juice
Tea
Water
qs.why: “Just water, thank you.”

qs.q: How long will the food take?
o: About twenty minutes
Only two minutes
About ten minutes
An hour
qs.why: “ready in about ten minutes”

qs.q: What is the dialogue mainly about?
o: A cooking teacher giving a class to a guest
A customer ordering lunch and asking about dairy
Two friends planning a picnic for the weekend
A chef changing the menu for a new season
qs.why: 음식 주문과 알레르기 확인이 중심이에요.

items.title: Weekend Plans
items.text:
Sam: Are you free this Saturday, Ben?
Ben: I think so. Why?
Sam: My cousin gave me two tickets to a baseball game. It starts at two o'clock.
Ben: That sounds great, but I have a dentist appointment in the morning.
Sam: How long will that take?
Ben: About an hour. I should be done by eleven.
Sam: Then we have plenty of time. Let's meet at the station at one.
Ben: Perfect. Should I bring some snacks?
Sam: Sure. I will buy the drinks at the stadium.

qs.q: Why did Sam call Ben?
o: To invite him to a baseball game
To ask him about the dentist
To plan a trip to a cousin's house
To sell him some snacks
qs.why: 야구 경기 티켓이 있어서 초대했어요.

qs.q: What is Ben doing on Saturday morning?
o: Watching a game
Meeting his cousin
Buying drinks
Visiting the dentist
qs.why: “I have a dentist appointment in the morning.”

qs.q: Where will they meet?
o: At the stadium
At the dentist's office
At the station
At Sam's house
qs.why: 역에서 한 시에 만나기로 했어요.

qs.q: What will Sam buy?
o: The snacks
The drinks
The tickets
The train fares
qs.why: “I will buy the drinks at the stadium.”

qs.q: Why does Sam say they have plenty of time?
o: Ben will be done before they meet.
The baseball game starts very late at night.
The station is right next to the big stadium.
Sam's cousin will drive them to the game.
qs.why: 11시에 끝나므로 1시 약속에 충분해요.

items.title: At the Lost and Found
items.text:
Clerk: Hello. How can I help you?
Mia: I lost my blue umbrella on the bus this morning.
Clerk: Which bus was it?
Mia: Number 33, around eight o'clock.
Clerk: Let me check. Is there anything special about it?
Mia: It has a small yellow duck on the handle.
Clerk: Ah, I think we have it. Please wait a moment.
Mia: Oh, thank you so much!
Clerk: Here it is. Could you sign this form, please?
Mia: Of course. I am really glad I came.

qs.q: What did Mia lose?
o: A bus ticket
A yellow duck
A school bag
An umbrella
qs.why: 버스에서 파란 우산을 잃어버렸어요.

qs.q: How does the clerk know it is Mia's umbrella?
o: It has her name on it.
It is the only blue one.
It has a small duck on the handle.
It was found on bus 33.
qs.why: Mia가 손잡이의 오리 장식을 설명했어요.

qs.q: What does Mia have to do at the end?
o: Pay a small fee
Sign a form
Call the bus driver
Wait until tomorrow
qs.why: “Could you sign this form, please?”

qs.q: How does Mia feel at the end?
o: Relieved and thankful
Angry and tired
Worried and afraid
Bored and quiet
qs.why: 되찾아서 기뻐하고 고마워해요.

qs.q: When did Mia lose the umbrella?
o: At a store near the station
After school last week
On the way to the museum
On the morning bus
qs.why: “this morning ... around eight”

items.title: Joining a Club
items.text:
Hana: Hi, Mr. Lee. I would like to join the science club.
Mr. Lee: Welcome, Hana. Do you have any experience?
Hana: Not really, but I enjoy watching nature videos.
Mr. Lee: That is a good start. We meet on Tuesdays and Thursdays.
Hana: I have piano lessons on Thursdays. Is Tuesday enough?
Mr. Lee: Yes, you can come on Tuesdays only. This month we are building small rockets.
Hana: Wow, that sounds exciting! Do I need to bring anything?
Mr. Lee: Just a notebook and a pencil. We will give you everything else.

qs.q: Why can't Hana come on Thursdays?
o: She has a science test.
She goes to nature camp.
She has piano lessons.
She helps her teacher.
qs.why: 목요일에는 피아노 수업이 있어요.

qs.q: What is the club doing this month?
o: Watching nature videos
Building small rockets
Visiting a museum
Planting a garden
qs.why: 이번 달에는 작은 로켓을 만들어요.

qs.q: What does Hana need to bring?
o: A notebook and a pencil
A piano book and a pencil
A nature video and a notebook
A small rocket and a notebook
qs.why: 공책과 연필만 가져오면 돼요.

qs.q: What can we infer about Mr. Lee?
o: He dislikes nature videos.
He teaches the piano.
He will close the club.
He welcomes beginners.
qs.why: 경험이 없는 Hana를 환영해요.

qs.q: How does Hana feel about the rockets?
o: Worried
Bored
Excited
Surprised by the cost
qs.why: “Wow, that sounds exciting!”

items.title: A Visit to the Doctor
items.text:
Doctor: Good morning, Tom. What seems to be the problem?
Tom: I have had a sore throat since Sunday, and I cough a lot at night.
Doctor: Do you have a fever?
Tom: A little. It was 37.8 this morning.
Doctor: Let me look. Open your mouth, please. Your throat is red. You have a cold.
Tom: Do I need medicine?
Doctor: Only some cough syrup. Drink plenty of warm water and rest for two days.
Tom: Can I go to school tomorrow?
Doctor: I would wait until Thursday so that you can get better.

qs.q: What is Tom's problem?
o: A broken arm
A sore throat and a cough
A headache and a toothache
A stomachache
qs.why: 목이 아프고 밤에 기침을 해요.

qs.q: What does the doctor tell Tom to do?
o: Rest and drink warm water
Take strong medicine for a week
Go to school as usual
Eat cold food
qs.why: 따뜻한 물을 많이 마시고 이틀 쉬라고 했어요.

qs.q: When can Tom probably go back to school?
o: Tomorrow
On Sunday
Next month
On Thursday
qs.why: 목요일까지 기다리라고 했어요.

qs.q: What is the doctor's opinion of Tom's illness?
o: It is very dangerous.
It needs an operation.
It is not serious.
It was caused by a dog.
qs.why: 가벼운 감기이고 기침약만 처방했어요.

qs.q: What is the dialogue mainly about?
o: A doctor going on holiday
A boy getting advice about a cold
A school's health rules
A new kind of cough syrup
qs.why: 감기에 대한 진료와 조언이 중심이에요.

items.title: Planning a Group Project
items.text:
Yuri: We need to finish our presentation on recycling by Friday.
David: Let's divide the work. I can do the research.
Yuri: Good. I will make the slides. Who will present?
Emma: I would like to, but I get nervous in front of people.
David: Maybe we can all speak for a few minutes. Then no one has to do it alone.
Emma: That would help me a lot.
Yuri: Great idea. Let's meet tomorrow after school to practice.
David: I have soccer practice until five. Can we meet at five thirty?
Yuri: Fine. See you in the library.

qs.q: Why does Emma hesitate to present?
o: She feels nervous in front of people.
She has no time left to do the research.
She dislikes the topic of recycling very much.
She has soccer practice every afternoon.
qs.why: 사람들 앞에서 긴장한다고 했어요.

qs.q: What will David do?
o: Make the slides
Present alone
Book the library
Do the research
qs.why: 자료 조사를 맡았어요.

qs.q: How do they solve the presenting problem?
o: Yuri will present the whole talk alone.
They will ask the teacher to choose a speaker.
Each person will speak for a short time.
They will change the topic of the talk.
qs.why: 모두가 조금씩 나눠서 발표해요.

qs.q: When and where will they practice?
o: Tomorrow at 5:00 in the gym
Tomorrow at 5:30 in the library
On Friday at 5:30 in the library
Tomorrow at 4:00 at the field
qs.why: 축구 연습이 5시에 끝나서 5시 30분이에요.

qs.q: What is the dialogue mainly about?
o: Students dividing the work for a talk
Students choosing a soccer team for Friday
A teacher grading a test about recycling
A library that is closing earlier than usual
qs.why: 조별 발표 준비를 나누는 대화예요.

items.q:
Read the notice and choose the best title.

“Many students leave their umbrellas at school on sunny days. After a week, the umbrella stand is full. Please check the stand and take your umbrella home today.”
o: A Sunny Week at School
Where to Buy an Umbrella
The Rain Is Coming Soon
Take Your Umbrella Home
items.why: 안내문은 학교에 두고 간 우산을 가져가라고 요청해요.

items.q:
What is the main idea of this paragraph?

“A small robot in our school helps the librarian. It carries heavy books from the desk to the shelves. It also tells visitors where to find a book by following a map on its screen. Now the librarian has more time to talk with students.”
o: Librarians will soon lose all of their jobs.
Heavy books are no longer allowed in the library.
A robot helps the library work more easily.
Students must learn to read maps in the library.
items.why: 로봇이 도서관 일을 돕는다는 것이 중심 내용이에요.

items.q:
According to the schedule, when does the drawing class end?

“Art Class Schedule: Painting 9:00-10:00, break 10:00-10:15, drawing 10:15-11:15, clay 11:15-12:00.”
items.why: 드로잉은 10:15에 시작해서 11:15에 끝나요.

items.q:
What can we infer from the text?

“Jisu looked at the clock again and again. The movie started in ten minutes, but her friend was still not there. She took out her phone and began to type a message.”
o: Jisu is waiting and feels uneasy.
Jisu has already seen the movie twice before.
Jisu is happy to watch the movie alone.
Jisu forgot where the cinema was located.
items.why: 시계를 계속 보고 메시지를 쓰는 모습에서 친구를 기다리며 초조함을 알 수 있어요.

items.q:
In the sentence below, what does “it” refer to?

“My uncle gave me a camera for my birthday. It has a long lens, so I can take pictures of birds from far away.”
o: My uncle
My birthday
The birds
The camera
items.why: it은 앞 문장의 a camera를 가리켜요.

items.q:
Which word is closest in meaning to “delighted” in the sentence?

“The children were delighted when the teacher said they could watch a movie.”
o: very tired
a little afraid
very happy
quite confused
items.why: 영화를 볼 수 있어 아주 기뻐했다는 뜻이에요.

items.q:
Why did the writer write this message?

“Hi Mina! I'm sorry I missed your call last night. My phone was in my bag. Can we talk after school tomorrow?”
o: To invite Mina to a birthday party
To apologize and suggest a time to talk
To ask Mina to buy a brand new phone
To complain about the call that was late
items.why: 전화를 못 받아 사과하고 다음 대화 시간을 제안해요.

items.q:
Put the sentences in the best order.

(A) Then she poured it into a cup. (B) Dana boiled some water. (C) Finally, she added a little honey.
o: B - A - C
A - B - C
C - A - B
B - C - A
items.why: 먼저 물을 끓이고, 컵에 붓고, 마지막에 꿀을 넣는 순서예요.

items.q:
Which sentence does NOT belong in the paragraph?

“(1) Whales are the largest animals in the sea. (2) They breathe air, so they come to the surface. (3) Sharks have many rows of teeth. (4) A whale can stay under water for more than an hour.”
o: (1) Whales are the largest animals in the sea.
(2) They breathe air, so they come to the surface.
(4) A whale can stay under water for more than an hour.
(3) Sharks have many rows of teeth.
items.why: 나머지는 고래에 관한 이야기인데 (3)만 상어 이야기예요.

items.q:
Choose the best word for the blank.

“I studied hard for the test. ______, I got a good score.”
o: For example
In the end of
As a result
On the other hand
items.why: 열심히 공부한 것의 결과이므로 As a result(그 결과)가 알맞아요.

items.q:
Choose the best word for the blank.

“Tom likes spicy food. ______, his sister cannot eat it at all.”
o: Therefore
However
Also
For example
items.why: 앞뒤 내용이 대조되므로 However가 알맞아요.

items.q:
What kind of text is this?

“Mix two cups of flour with one cup of milk. Add one egg and stir well. Pour a little of the mixture into a hot pan and cook for one minute on each side.”
o: A recipe
A diary entry
A news report
An advertisement
items.why: 재료와 만드는 순서를 알려 주는 요리법이에요.

items.q:
What does the sign tell visitors?

“Please walk. Wet floor. Staff are cleaning this area.”
o: Close the door as quickly as you can.
Use the stairs if you want to go up.
Wait here for the staff to come back.
Take care because the floor is wet.
items.why: 젖은 바닥을 조심하라는 표지판이에요.

items.q:
What is the main idea of this paragraph?

“Walking to school has many benefits. It gives you exercise, wakes up your brain, and saves money on bus fares. You can also enjoy the fresh air and chat with friends on the way.”
o: Bus fares are too expensive for students.
Students should choose friends carefully.
Walking to school is good in many ways.
Fresh air is hard to find in cities.
items.why: 등교길 걷기의 여러 장점을 말해요.

items.q:
Why did Henry bring an umbrella?

“Henry checked the weather report in the morning. It said there would be heavy rain after lunch, so he put an umbrella in his bag.”
o: His bag was much too light to carry.
The report said that rain was coming.
He wanted to lend it to a classmate later.
It was a birthday present from his mother.
items.why: 일기예보에서 점심 후 비가 온다고 해서 챙겼어요.

items.q:
What does the writer want readers to do?

“Our park is losing its flowers because people pick them. If everyone picks just one, there will be none left for others. Please leave the flowers for everyone to enjoy.”
o: Leave the flowers in the park
Pick only one flower each day
Plant new flowers at their homes
Pay some money to enter the park
items.why: 꽃을 따지 말고 모두가 즐길 수 있게 두라는 부탁이에요.

items.q:
What is the best title for the text?

“Octopuses are very smart. They can open jars, find their way through mazes, and even change color to hide from enemies. Scientists are still learning how their brains work.”
o: How to Open a Jar
A Maze Under the Sea
Colors of the Rainbow
The Clever Octopus
items.why: 문어의 영리함을 소개하는 글이에요.

items.q:
According to the text, which is true?

“Mina's school starts at 8:40. She leaves home at 8:00 and takes bus 5 for fifteen minutes. Then she walks for ten minutes.”
o: Mina walks for fifteen minutes each way.
Mina's school starts at eight o'clock sharp.
Mina spends twenty-five minutes on the trip.
Mina takes bus 5 for only ten minutes.
items.why: 버스 15분 + 걷기 10분 = 25분이에요.

items.q:
What can we infer about the weather?

“Everyone in the street was wearing a thick coat and a scarf. Some people were blowing on their hands to keep them warm.”
o: It was very hot.
It was very cold.
It was windy but warm.
It was sunny and dry.
items.why: 두꺼운 외투와 목도리, 손을 불어 녹이는 모습에서 추운 날씨예요.

items.q:
What does “They” refer to in the second sentence?

“Dolphins live in groups called pods. They help each other find food and protect the young.”
o: Dolphins
Pods
The young
Fishers
items.why: They는 첫 문장의 Dolphins를 가리켜요.

items.q:
What does the word “crowded” mean in this sentence?

“The subway was so crowded that I could not find a seat.”
o: very clean and neat
too dark to see
far away from home
full of people
items.why: 자리를 못 찾을 만큼 사람이 많았다는 뜻이에요.

items.q:
Which sentence best summarizes the text?

“Lena wanted to buy a bike. She saved her allowance for six months and did small jobs for her neighbors. At last, she had enough money and bought a red bike.”
o: Lena received a bike from her neighbors.
Lena sold her old bike for money.
Lena worked and saved to buy a bike.
Lena lost her allowance on a bike.
items.why: 자전거를 사기 위해 용돈을 모으고 일을 한 이야기예요.

items.q:
What is the writer's feeling in this note?

“Thank you so much for helping me with my homework! I could not have finished it without you. You are a great friend.”
o: Jealous
Grateful
Disappointed
Embarrassed
items.why: 도움에 고마워하고 있어요.

items.q:
When can visitors enter the pool for free?

“Pool hours: Monday to Friday 6 a.m.-9 p.m. Saturday and Sunday 8 a.m.-6 p.m. Free entry for children under seven. Adults pay 3,000 won.”
o: Children under seven at any open time
Adults who come on the weekend mornings
Everyone who visits on a Monday evening
Teenagers who arrive after 9 p.m. closing
items.why: 7세 미만 어린이는 무료예요.

items.q:
Which statement is true?

“Tigers are the largest cats in the world. Unlike many cats, they love water and are good swimmers. Most tigers live alone and only meet others to mate or to raise young.”
o: Tigers live in large groups.
Tigers are afraid of water.
Tigers are smaller than lions.
Tigers can swim well.
items.why: 호랑이는 물을 좋아하고 수영을 잘해요.

items.q:
Choose the sentence that best fits the blank in the paragraph.

“Our town has many places to relax. ______ There are quiet parks, a long river path, and a small lake where people fish.”
o: It is hard to find free time.
Many shops open late at night.
You can enjoy nature close to home.
Winter comes early in the town.
items.why: 뒤에 공원, 강길, 호수가 나오므로 자연을 즐길 수 있다는 문장이 알맞아요.

items.q:
Which sentence introduces the topic of the paragraph?

“(1) Learning a language takes time. (2) Some people practice by watching films. (3) Others prefer to talk with friends. (4) Whatever the way, regular practice is the key.”
items.why: (1)이 단락의 주제(언어 학습에는 시간이 걸린다)를 처음 소개하는 문장이에요.

items.q:
What will Ben probably do next?

“Ben opened the fridge, but the milk was gone. His cereal was ready in the bowl, and he was already late for school.”
o: Find something else to put on his cereal
Go back to bed for another hour or so
Pour his cereal into the kitchen sink
Make a big pizza for his lunch box
items.why: 우유가 없으니 시리얼에 다른 것을 찾을 가능성이 높아요.

items.q:
Which sentence is closest in meaning to the text?

“I haven't seen Jiho since last Friday.”
o: I saw Jiho on Friday and again this morning.
I will see Jiho next Friday at school.
Jiho has been staying with me since Friday.
I last saw Jiho on Friday.
items.why: 지난 금요일 이후로 못 봤다는 뜻이에요.

items.q:
Why did the writer feel sad?

“My best friend is moving to another city next week. We have played together since we were five. I do not know who I will sit with at lunch.”
o: The writer lost a game.
The lunch was cancelled.
The best friend is moving away.
The writer has a new teacher.
items.why: 가장 친한 친구가 이사 가기 때문이에요.

items.q:
What is the best reply to the invitation?

“Hi Lisa, I am having a birthday party at my house on Saturday at 3 o'clock. Can you come?”
o: Happy birthday! You are old.
I'd love to come. What can I bring?
I went to the cinema yesterday.
Please give me your address book.
items.why: 초대에 대한 자연스러운 수락 답장이에요.

items.q:
What does the advertisement offer?

“Summer Sale! All swimsuits are 30% off from July 1 to July 7. Buy two and get a free towel!”
o: A free towel when buying two swimsuits
A free swimsuit when buying one large towel
A discount on towels for the whole summer
A sale that lasts from July until the end of August
items.why: 수영복 두 개를 사면 수건을 무료로 줘요.

items.q:
What is the writer's opinion?

“I think homework is useful, but teachers should not give too much. When students have two hours of homework every night, they have no time to rest or play.”
o: Homework should be stopped in all schools.
Students should be given more homework daily.
Teachers like to give no homework at all.
Homework is useful, but too much is bad.
items.why: 유용하지만 너무 많으면 문제라는 의견이에요.

items.q:
What happened first in the story?

“We stayed in and played cards while it rained. After the rain stopped, we went out to the garden. There we found a rainbow over the roof.”
o: They found a rainbow.
They went to the garden.
They played cards.
The rain stopped.
items.why: 비가 오는 동안 실내에서 카드놀이를 했고, 그다음에 비가 그쳐서 정원에 나갔어요.

items.q:
What does the expression “break the ice” most likely mean here?

“At the new class party, Jack told a funny story to break the ice, and soon everyone was talking.”
o: To make ice for the cold drinks
To help people feel at ease together
To end the party much earlier than planned
To tell a scary story to the new students
items.why: 어색한 분위기를 풀다라는 뜻의 관용 표현이에요.

items.q:
What is the main purpose of this text?

“Dear neighbors, the elevator will be repaired on Thursday from 10 a.m. to 3 p.m. Please use the stairs during that time. We are sorry for the trouble.”
o: To tell residents about the elevator repair
To ask people to buy a new elevator
To explain how elevators work
To invite neighbors to a party
items.why: 엘리베이터 수리 일정을 알려 주는 안내문이에요.

items.q:
According to the passage, why do plants need sunlight?

“Plants use sunlight, water, and air to make their own food. Without light, the leaves cannot do this work and the plant slowly becomes weak.”
o: They use it to drink water.
They use it to move to new places.
They use it to make soil.
They use it to make food.
items.why: 햇빛은 식물이 양분을 만드는 데 쓰여요.

items.q:
Which title fits the text best?

“Gwen woke up early and went to the beach with her father. They sat on a rock and watched the sun slowly come up out of the sea. The sky turned pink, then gold.”
o: A Night at the Cinema
Learning to Swim
A Beautiful Sunrise
Fishing with Friends
items.why: 일출을 보는 내용이에요.

items.good: Although it was raining, we played outside.
bad: Although it was raining, but we played outside.
Although it was raining, we play outside yesterday.
Although it was raining we plays outside.

cz.st: ___ it was raining, we played outside.

items.rule: Although는 ‘~이지만’이라는 양보의 접속사이고, 같은 문장에서 but과 함께 쓰지 않아요.
items.hint: 문장 앞뒤 내용이 서로 반대되는지 생각해 보세요.

items.good: The book that I borrowed was very interesting.
bad: The book who I borrowed was very interesting.
The book what I borrowed was very interesting.
The book that I borrowed it was very interesting.

cz.st: The book ___ I borrowed was very interesting.

items.rule: 사물을 꾸미는 관계대명사는 that이나 which를 써요. who는 사람에게 쓰고, 관계대명사가 목적어 역할을 하면 it을 따로 쓰지 않아요.

items.good: The letter was written by my grandmother.
bad: The letter written by my grandmother.
The letter was wrote by my grandmother.
The letter wrote by my grandmother.

cz.st: The letter was ___ by my grandmother.

items.good: I have lived in this town for five years.
items.ko: 나는 이 마을에서 5년 동안 살고 있다.
bad: I live in this town for five years ago.
I am living in this town since five years.
I have lived in this town five years ago.

cz.st: I have lived in this town ___ five years.

items.rule: 기간(five years)에는 for를 쓰고, 시작 시점에는 since를 써요. 현재완료는 ago와 함께 쓰지 않아요.

items.good: It was so cold that we stayed at home.
bad: It was so cold which we stayed at home.
It was so cold what we stayed at home.
It was such cold that we stayed at home.

cz.st: It was so cold ___ we stayed at home.

items.good: She asked me where I had bought the bag.
items.ko: 그녀는 내가 그 가방을 어디서 샀는지 물었다.
bad: She asked me where had I bought the bag.
She asked me where did I buy the bag.
She asked me where I buy the bag yesterday.

cz.st: She asked me where I ___ the bag.

items.rule: 간접의문문은 ‘의문사 + 주어 + 동사’ 순서이고, 과거 이전의 일은 과거완료로 나타낼 수 있어요.

items.good: I'm happy to hear the good news.
bad: I'm happy hearing to the good news.
I'm happy for hear the good news.
I'm happy hear the good news.
items.rule: 감정을 나타내는 형용사 뒤에 to부정사를 써서 그 감정의 원인을 말할 수 있어요.

items.good: This lake is the deepest in the country.
bad: This lake is deeper in the country.
This lake is the most deep in the country.
This lake is deepest than the country.

cz.st: This lake is the ___ in the country.

items.rule: 짧은 형용사의 최상급은 the + 형용사-est로 만들어요.

items.good: If you read the question first, you can find the answer easily.
items.ko: 질문을 먼저 읽으면 답을 쉽게 찾을 수 있다.
bad: If you will read the question first, you can find the answer easily.
If you reading the question first, you can find the answer easily.
If you read the question first, you can found the answer easily.

cz.st: If you read the question first, you ___ find the answer easily.

items.rule: 조건절에서는 미래의 일도 현재 시제로 쓰고, can 뒤에는 동사원형이 와요.

items.good: My brother, who lives in Busan, is a nurse.
bad: My brother, which lives in Busan, is a nurse.
My brother, who live in Busan, is a nurse.
My brother, he lives in Busan, is a nurse.

cz.st: My brother, ___ lives in Busan, is a nurse.

items.rule: 사람을 설명하는 주격 관계대명사는 who이고, 단수 선행사이므로 동사는 lives예요.

items.good: I forgot to bring my umbrella, so I got wet.
items.ko: 우산을 가져오는 것을 잊어서 비를 맞았다.
bad: I forgot bringing my umbrella, so I got wet.
I forgot to bring my umbrella, because I got wet.
I forgot to bring my umbrella, but so I got wet.

cz.st: I forgot ___ my umbrella, so I got wet.

items.rule: forget to-부정사는 ‘~할 것을 잊다’, forget -ing는 ‘~했던 것을 잊다’라는 뜻이에요.
